questions.explain: The chapter's evidence contract: the copilot answers from live telemetry via read-only tools plus runbooks/incident history as quoted excerpts; model memory and generic advice must be labeled as such.
options: Model training memory and public documentation
Live telemetry pulled through read-only tools, and the team's own runbooks and incident history retrieved as quoted excerpts
The SQL Server error log and Windows Event Viewer only
Stack Overflow answers cached in a table
questions.q: What are the two evidence sources a DBA copilot may answer from?

questions.explain: The chapter is explicit: the model selects tools and parameters but never concatenates its own T-SQL, keeping execution bounded and safe.
options: Because free-form SQL from an LLM risks injection vulnerabilities and unpredictable behavior — every database interaction must go through a fixed, parameterized tool template executed under a least-privilege login
Because pyodbc cannot execute dynamic SQL
Because it would make answers too slow
Because SQL Server rejects AI-generated queries
questions.q: Why must the LLM never write free-form SQL in the copilot design?

questions.explain: The system prompt rule: no cited runbook, no procedure — operational answers without a runbook citation are treated as drafts, never guidance.
options: It may improvise procedures from training data if no runbook is found
It should ask the user to search the wiki themselves
It must quote the relevant runbook excerpt and cite its document ID — and decline procedural guidance if no runbook excerpt was retrieved
It must always escalate to PagerDuty
questions.q: What rule governs the copilot's answers about operational procedures like failovers?

questions.explain: The tool queries sys.dm_exec_sessions to validate the target and blocks auto-kill for sessions holding open transactions, routing those to DBA approval.
options: It checks the session's last backup date
It verifies the session holds no locks
It emails the session owner first
It confirms the session exists, is a user process (session_id > 50, is_user_process = 1), and refuses to auto-kill when open_transaction_count > 0
questions.q: What pre-flight validation does the kill-session action tool perform?

questions.explain: Tool precision (right tools called), grounding rate (claims trace to tool output), and abstention quality (declines when data is insufficient); confident wrong answers are the failure mode that matters.
options: Latency, throughput, and availability
Tool precision, grounding rate, and abstention quality — with the rollout bar set on the weakest metric
Code coverage, bug count, and uptime
Token cost, model size, and context length
questions.q: What three metrics does the golden question set score before rollout?
